terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the setup to build the repository, then work inside repo/ with git.

tasks.title: Bring back the deleted branch
tasks.description:
Run `node setup.mjs`, then work inside `repo/`.

The branch `harbour-alerts` held three unmerged commits by Pavel and was deleted. Recreate it.

The check expects:

- a branch named exactly `harbour-alerts`
- it contains all three of Pavel's commits
- it points at exactly the last commit the branch had before it was deleted, with nothing new on top
nextSteps: Run `node setup.mjs`, then `cd repo` and `git reflog`.
Find the last commit HEAD made while it was on harbour-alerts.
Look at that commit with `git show` before you use it.
Create the branch at that commit and list it with `git log --oneline harbour-alerts`.
hints: Deleting a branch removes a name, not the commits. Something still remembers where HEAD has been.
In the reflog, the checkout line that says it moved from harbour-alerts to main tells you which entry just below it is the branch's last commit.
`git branch <name> <hash>` creates a branch at any commit. Use the hash of the newest commit Pavel made on that branch.

tasks.title: Undo the reset on main
tasks.description:
`main` was reset two commits too far, dropping `Add winter timetable note` and `Add bike rack notice`. Put `main` back.

The check expects:

- `main` points at the commit it pointed at just before the reset
- `README.md` and `timetable.txt` on `main` match that commit
- the working tree is clean and nothing is left half done
nextSteps: Run `git reflog show main` and find the reset line.
Identify where main was one move before the reset.
Move main there, files included, then run `git status` and `git log --oneline`.
hints: The reset itself is in the reflog. The entry just below it is where main stood before.
You can name that moment without copying a hash: the reflog syntax `main@{n}`.
While on main, a hard reset to the reflog entry from before the reset moves the branch and the files together. Then `git status` should be clean.
